rules.sentence: Blood cultures are positive in 30–78% of cases of pyogenic spondylodiscitis.

It must be noted that these biological features can be missing with tubercular spondylodiscitis and intracellular development microorganisms (such as Brucella spp., Legionella spp., and Listeria spp.).
An early imaging diagnosis is usually considered the detection of the disease when only minor vertebral and disk damages are present.
Changes in pyogenic spondylitis are not apparent on plain radiographs until 2–8 weeks after the initial symptoms.
CRP is more sensitive as a marker for treatment response, with a drop of 50% per week, and is a good predictor for disease treatment.
